title: Large language model psychometrics: A systematic review of evaluation, validation, and enhancement

bias_targets.methodology: Administering standardized political science questionnaires and surveys (e.g., ANES, ATP, PCT, GLES) to map LLMs on multidimensional political spectrums and evaluate their responses for ideological leanings or Western-centric tendencies.

Applying psychometric tools like the Cognitive Reflection Test (CRT), synthetic scenarios, and multi-agent dialogues to measure heuristics and systematic errors such as anchoring, framing, loss aversion, and the conjunction fallacy.

Comparing direct self-report responses against indirect or contextual prompts to identify skewed preferences toward socially acceptable or favorable traits (e.g., inflated extraversion or lowered neuroticism).

Conducting cross-lingual psychometric tests to identify inconsistencies in personality trait measurements and cognitive abilities across different languages, highlighting Western-centric alignment in models.
Analyzing systematic answer patterns in structured multiple-choice tests, such as consistently favoring a specific option letter (e.g., 'A') regardless of the actual content of the item.
